objects.original: One standard Euclidean Brownian motion with its filtration, two distinct coordinate processes, predictable dyadic weight arrays, and a common second-moment bound.
objects.reconstructed: Measurable Omega with measure mu and filtration F; finite Euclidean coordinate type kappa; standard Brownian B; distinct coordinates j,k; horizon T; real triangular array w_{n,i}; common real bound C.

domains.original: Finite coordinate set with decidable equality; real predictable weights on each of 2^n cells of a fixed horizon T≥0; arbitrary measurable sample space with the given measure and filtration.
domains.reconstructed: kappa finite with decidable equality. B:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^kappa; j,k∈kappa, j≠k; T≥0. For n∈N, i ranges from 0 to 2^n-1 and w_{n,i}:Omega→R. mu has no explicit IsFiniteMeasure instance in the target.

assumptions.original: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration. Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint. One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.
assumptions.reconstructed: Assumptions: B is standard Brownian with F: starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent disjoint-interval increments, centered Gaussian projections with variance (t-s)||ell||² for s<t, and a.e. continuous paths; B is strongly adapted and each B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. Each weight w_{n,i} is strongly measurable with respect to F_{iT/2^n}, the left-endpoint sigma-algebra and is in L²(mu). For every n,i, ∫w_{n,i}² dmu≤C. No positivity of T or C, no usual-filtration condition, and no independence of weights from the full path is separately assumed.

conclusion.original: For two distinct coordinates of one Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted dyadic mixed increment sum is in L² at each level and converges to zero in mean square. Formula: C_n=\sum_i w_{n,i}\Delta_i B^j\,\Delta_i B^k,\qquad C_n\in L^2,\qquad \mathbb E[C_n^2]\longrightarrow0.
conclusion.reconstructed: Conclusion: Let t_i^n=iT/2^n, Delta_i^n B^j=B^j(t_{i+1}^n)-B^j(t_i^n), and E_n=∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}w_{n,i} Delta_i^n B^j Delta_i^n B^k. Then E_n∈L²(mu) for every n, and ∫ E_n² dmu→0.

quantifiers.original: For all given Brownian data, distinct coordinates, horizon, weights and uniform bound C, every level sum lies in L² and its squared integral tends to zero.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Quantifier order: For all data, distinct j,k, T, weights and real C satisfying the hypotheses, every level error is in L² and its second moment tends to zero as n→infinity.

scopes.original: Mean-square convergence on the full dyadic sequence at a fixed possibly zero horizon; no almost-sure convergence or rate claimed. Predictability refers to the left-endpoint sigma-algebra.
scopes.reconstructed: Scope: Convergence of second moments, hence L² convergence of the error to zero. A fixed possibly zero horizon and the entire dyadic sequence are used; no a.e. convergence or rate is asserted.

constant_dependencies.original: C is supplied uniformly over levels and cells; no additional constant or rate appears in the conclusion.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Constant dependencies: C is one given bound uniform over n and i. No further constant is selected in the conclusion.
